rule: Every statement of the contract is stated in Lean, Coq and Agda and tested in Haskell, each entry naming its declaration, or the entry gives the reason the language cannot state it. scripts/check_formal_parity.py fails on a missing declaration, on a contract-module declaration in no statement, and when absent entries exceed max_absent. The Rust runtime relies only on statements whose Lean, Coq and Agda entries are present.

statements.statement: a measurement with feedback: bath, external work, free-energy change
the process family: erasure, measurement with feedback, gate transition
the prior a process is judged against: erasure, feedback, state move, transformation
the one second law SecondLaw : Process → Prior → Prop
SI Clausius form ΔS ≤ W/(k_B T) with the exact k_B
the erase instance at work W in units of k_B·K is exactly the SI Clausius form at k_B·W joules
a prior of the wrong kind is refused
the erasure dissipating T ln 2 obeys the law for a uniform bit (Agda: for every entropy drop ΔS of the prior; the uniform bit is ΔS = ln 2)
the Landauer bound T ln 2 ≤ W for a uniform bit (Agda: for every entropy drop ΔS of the prior; the uniform bit is ΔS = ln 2)
the SI Landauer bound k_B T ln 2 ≤ W (Agda: for every entropy drop ΔS of the prior; the uniform bit is ΔS = ln 2)
the Szilard joint distribution (one bit of correlation)
its first marginal is uniform
its second marginal is uniform
its joint entropy is ln 2
its mutual information is ln 2
the Szilard engine at temperature T
the Szilard engine obeys the second law at equality
a state move that changes nothing is admissible
the predicate is satisfiable (it is not vacuous)
binary erasure is the transformation whose target is the Dirac state
leaving a distribution unchanged costs nothing
transformations compose: entropy drops telescope, costs add
a thermochemical update: bath, distributions before and after, work, defect
structural coherence: zero defect
the erasure that pays for an update
the entropy an update removes
the chemical second law: a coherent update whose erasure obeys SecondLaw on its transformation
the chemical second law is the Clausius bound ΔS ≤ W/T on the assemblage
coherent updates compose under the one second law
the work floor T·ΔS of a refinement
an update's work meets its floor
at a positive bath temperature the Landauer floor T·ΔS ≤ W is the Clausius bound ΔS ≤ W / T
a coherent update obeys the chemical second law exactly when its work meets the Landauer floor of its entropy drop
a binary assemblage erasure realised by an erasure process
the erasure instance bounds the bridged update's entropy drop
a bridged update dissipates at least T ln 2
a bridged coherent update obeys the chemical second law
the coherent P0 fixture update
the P0 fixture removes no entropy
the P0 fixture is coherent
the P0 fixture obeys the chemical second law
independent erasures: the entropy both remove is at most the entropy both dissipate
the Powers volume coefficients derived from the cited water parameters conserve volume
at every initial water fraction and degree of hydration the Powers phases fill the paste
per unit volume of cement, capillary water remains at complete hydration exactly when w ≥ (w/c)* = 0.42
per unit volume of cement, the hydration products fit at complete hydration exactly when w ≥ (w/c)_s = 0.356
cement admissibility is the transition instance of the second law with hydration and strength non-decreasing
a step the cement gate passes is a member of the second-law predicate
for Helmholtz states within the mass tolerance, a step is a member of the second-law predicate exactly when hydration does not go backwards
selection under cost: the evidence-tagged candidate of least global free energy, ties by id, when it lowers the source's free energy; a residue otherwise
selection over no candidates returns the residue noCandidates
the selected candidate is an evidence-tagged member and no evidence-tagged candidate has lower global free energy
the selected candidate's global free energy is strictly below the source's
selection does not depend on the order of candidates with distinct ids
every candidate move of a cement state is a member of the second-law predicate (so is the candidate selection returns)
the second law as one inequality: ΔF ≤ W_in + k_B·T·I
admissible steps at a common bath temperature compose (free energy, work and information add)
the erase instance is the one inequality with I = 0
the measurement-with-feedback instance is the one inequality with W_in = −W_ext
the transition instance is the one inequality with W_in = 0 and I = 0, with the mass condition
an admissible transition followed by an admissible erase composes at the erase's bath
every member of the one predicate packages as a step obeying the one inequality
the Szilard cycle (measure one bit, then erase it) composes at the bath
under the Esposito conditions fine erase admissibility implies coarse erase admissibility
the identity coarse graining meets the Esposito conditions
a refused coarse erasure refuses the fine one
erasing a product pair admits erasing its first factor (H(X) ≤ H(X,Y))
the Esposito conditions are satisfiable
the semantic second law: consistency, the Clausius bound on the shared model, and information preserved above a threshold
the semantic second law is the one predicate on the shared model with consistency and preserved information
the erase instance discharges the entropy clause of a physically bridged transition
a consistent, information-preserving, physically bridged transition obeys the semantic second law
the consistent identity transition has no uncertainty drop
a product proposal–outcome witness carries no mutual information
an erasure obeying the predicate dissipates at least k_B T times the entropy it removes, in joules
an erasure obeying the predicate removes at most 1/(k_B T) nats per joule (Agda states it with the denominators cleared, as the joule bound)
erasing b bits to a point under the predicate costs at least b k_B T ln 2 joules (Agda carries the information of one bit as data)
a claim of b bits paid by an erasure of b bits obeying the predicate spends honestly
an honest claim's information-per-joule score is at most its dignity over the Landauer bit energy (Agda: denominators cleared)
a claim paid by an erasure obeying the predicate scores at most its dignity over the Landauer bit energy (Agda: denominators cleared)

a history move is admissible under the one predicate exactly when the entropy of the erased distribution is at most the work over the bath temperature (Agda carries the erased distribution by its entropy and the erasure by the entropy W/T it dissipates, so the bound reads erased entropy ≤ dissipated entropy)
Kleisli composition of history head moves is associative at every state
the Kleisli identity is a left unit of composition at every state
the Kleisli identity is a right unit of composition at every state
a move that preserves provenance extends the stamp chain by the prior commit
a move that preserves provenance retains a held second-law witness (the Haskell witness slot is a Boolean)
an admissible history move from the prior's commit preserves provenance; the one predicate discharges the witness (the Haskell witness slot is a Boolean)
a mode storing ½·k·s² (s ≠ 0) whose passive relaxation to the natural state obeys the second law (transition case) has k ≥ 0 (Agda: the squared strain enters as a positive rational q)

a body held at stress σ ≠ 0 by a modulus E ≠ 0 stores σ²/(2E); its passive relaxation under the second law forces E > 0 (Agda: the stored energy ψ is given by 2·E·ψ = σ², σ² a positive rational, and E ≠ 0 follows)
two quadratic modes ½·a·x² + ½·b·y² relaxing passively under the second law from every (x, y) have a ≥ 0 and b ≥ 0

an isotropic solid storing ½·K·e² + ½·G·γ² relaxing passively under the second law from every volumetric strain and shear, with 3K + G > 0, has −1 ≤ ν ≤ 1/2 for ν = (3K − 2G)/(2(3K + G)) (Agda: the denominator cleared, −2(3K + G) ≤ 3K − 2G ≤ 3K + G)
under the same relaxation Young's modulus E = 9KG/(3K + G) is nonnegative (Agda: the denominator cleared, 9·K·G ≥ 0)
a standard linear solid storing ½·G∞·ε² + ½·G₁·ξ² relaxing passively under the second law from every total and arm strain has 0 ≤ G∞ ≤ G∞ + G₁ = G₀

an orthotropic lamina with nonzero moduli relaxing passively under the second law from every plane stress state has E₁ > 0, E₂ > 0 and ν₁₂² ≤ E₁/E₂ (Agda: on the compliance entries with S₂₂ > 0, S₁₂² ≤ S₁₁·S₂₂)
a passive step dissipating c·q (q > 0) out of the free energy obeys the second law (transition case) only when c ≥ 0
a dashpot at rate r ≠ 0 over dt > 0 dissipating η·r²·dt obeys the second law only when η ≥ 0 (Agda: r² enters as a positive rational q)
a Bingham fluid dissipating (τ₀·|r| + η_p·r²)·dt that obeys the second law at every rate has τ₀ ≥ 0 and η_p ≥ 0 (Agda: at every positive rate, where |r| = r)
a harmonic strain cycle dissipating π·E″·ε₀² (ε₀ ≠ 0) obeys the second law only when E″ ≥ 0, and then E″/E′ ≥ 0 for E′ > 0 (Coq, Agda: the cycle measure π·ε₀² enters as a positive rational q)
a passive impact with free energy ½·μ·v² before and ½·μ·(e·v)² after that obeys the second law (transition case) has e ≤ 1 for e ≥ 0 and μ·v² > 0 (Agda: μ·v² enters as a positive rational m)
the kinetic energy lost in such an impact, ½·μ·v²·(1 − e²), is nonnegative
the uniform bit carries ln 2 nats: H(½, ½) = log 2
the upper end of the dignity range [0, d_max] is 10
with both steps honest, the dignity step is monotone in the claimed information
Gaussian mutual information in bits from the correlation: MI(ρ) = −½·log₂(1 − ρ²) for ρ² < 1
the default window W = 32 warms up after max 3 ⌈√32⌉ = 6 samples, at least the reference count ⌈2·ln 4⌉
erasing the uniform bit with work per kelvin r obeys the second law exactly when ln 2 ≤ r
ln 2 is the least work per kelvin the second law admits for erasing one uniform bit
a vacuum field storing ½·ε·E² relaxes passively from every field exactly when ε ≥ 0
a field storing B²/(2μ), μ ≠ 0, relaxes passively from every flux density exactly when μ > 0
every Joule step dissipating G·V²·dt is admitted exactly when the conductance G ≥ 0
every Joule step dissipating R·I²·dt is admitted exactly when the resistance R ≥ 0
at the exact SI ε₀ every vacuum field relaxes under the second law (ε₀ inside the bound ε ≥ 0)
at the exact SI μ₀ every vacuum field relaxes under the second law (μ₀ inside the bound μ > 0)
at the exact G₀ = 2e²/h every Joule step is admitted (G₀ inside the bound G ≥ 0)
at the exact R_K = h/e² every Joule step is admitted (R_K inside the bound R ≥ 0)
a plastic strain and a hardening variable storing ½·k·(x² + y² + 2c·x·y) that relax from every (x, y), with k ≠ 0, have k > 0 and −1 ≤ c ≤ 1 (Agda: takes k > 0 and states 0 ≤ 1 + c and 0 ≤ 1 − c)
a phase field φ ∉ {0, 1} storing k·φ²·(1 − φ)² that relaxes has k ≥ 0 (Agda: the envelope enters as a positive rational q)
a crack extension ΔA > 0 dissipating G_c·ΔA obeys the second law only when G_c ≥ 0
with G_c ≥ 0 from a crack extension and E > 0 from an elastic relaxation, K = √(E·G_c) ≥ 0 and K² = E·G_c (Coq and Agda: the radicand E·G_c ≥ 0)
steady creep at stress σ > 0 with rate A·σⁿ over dt > 0 dissipates σ·A·σⁿ·dt and obeys the second law only when A ≥ 0 (Coq and Agda: σⁿ enters as a positive rational p)
a scale of thickness x > 0 growing at k_p/(2x) under a reaction affinity a > 0 dissipates a·k_p/(2x)·dt and obeys the second law only when k_p ≥ 0 (Agda: 1/(2x) enters as a positive rational w)
a fibre with bond stress b·√f_c (f_c > 0) sliding over a slip area s > 0 dissipates b·√f_c·s and obeys the second law only when b ≥ 0 (Coq and Agda: √f_c enters as a positive rational r)
a reaction with affinity A > 0 advancing at rate ξ̇ over dt > 0 dissipates A·ξ̇·dt and obeys the second law only when ξ̇ ≥ 0
with affinity A > 0 and rate law ξ̇ = k·g, g > 0, the step dissipates A·(k·g)·dt and obeys the second law only when k ≥ 0
Fickian diffusion at a gradient g ≠ 0 with thermodynamic factor χ > 0 over dt > 0 dissipates D·χ·g²·dt and obeys the second law only when D ≥ 0 (Agda: g² enters as a positive rational q)

Darcy flow at a pressure gradient g ≠ 0 through a fluid of viscosity μ > 0 over dt > 0 dissipates (κ/μ)·g²·dt and obeys the second law only when κ ≥ 0 (Agda: 1/μ enters as a positive fluidity f and g² as a positive q)
with K = K_s·(1 − b), b − φ = K_s·n and K_s > 0, a drained mode ½·K·s² and a pore mode ½·n·s² that relax passively give φ ≤ b ≤ 1

with m = n + φ·c_f, φ > 0 and c_f ≠ 0, a pore mode ½·n·s² and a fluid mode ½·c_f·s² that relax passively give a storage coefficient m = 1/M > 0 and a Biot modulus M > 0 (Coq and Lean also conclude M > 0 from M·m = 1; Agda states m > 0)

an isotropic solid storing ½·K·e² + ½·G·γ² with K ≠ 0 and G ≠ 0 that relaxes passively from every (e, γ) has K > 0, G > 0 and −1 < ν < 1/2 (Agda: the Poisson bounds with the positive denominator cleared)

every dissipation-potential expression (PSD quadratic, |x|, |x|^p with p ≥ 1, Norton a·|x|^(m+1), nonnegative scaling, sum, max, linear precomposition) denotes φ with φ(0) = 0 (Lean over Fin n → ℝ with real exponents p ≥ 1, m ≥ 0; Coq, Agda and Haskell over one rational rate with natural exponents)
every expression denotes φ ≥ 0
every expression denotes φ convex: φ(t·x + (1 − t)·y) ≤ t·φ(x) + (1 − t)·φ(y) for t ∈ [0, 1] (Haskell: random chords in exact rationals)
for a subgradient g of an expression's φ at the rate x, φ(x) ≤ g·x and the dissipation g·x is nonnegative (Lean states it for every PassivePotential)
a step dissipating g·x (g a subgradient of a grammar potential) under the passive balance (ψ_new − ψ_old) + g·x ≤ 0 and the mass condition is a transition case of SecondLaw
the capped potential min(|x|, 1), nonnegative and zero at zero but not convex, is the denotation of no expression (Haskell: its chord inequality fails at x = 0, y = 2, t = ½)

with L antisymmetric, M symmetric positive semidefinite, L·∇S = 0 and M·∇E = 0, the energy rate ∇E·(L∇E + M∇S) is zero (Lean over Fin n → ℝ with Mathlib matrices; Coq and Agda over n rational coordinates; Haskell over exact rationals with operators built to satisfy the conditions)
under the GENERIC conditions the entropy rate ∇S·(L∇E + M∇S) equals ∇S·M∇S and is nonnegative

read at a reservoir temperature T ≥ 0 with free energy ψ = E − T·S and endpoint states meeting the mass condition, a GENERIC step is a transition case of SecondLaw (Lean: along a differentiable trajectory from t₀ to t₁ ≥ t₀, with E constant and S nondecreasing; Coq, Agda and Haskell: a step of length h ≥ 0 whose ψ changes by h times the free-energy rate)

GSM cartridges (dissipation potentials convex, non-negative, zero at zero) form a commutative monoid under pointwise sum, closed under non-negative scaling (Lean: AddCommMonoid and ℝ≥0-module over ℝ; Coq, Agda and Haskell: the monoid and cone laws pointwise over the rationals, potentials in supporting-line form)

the dissipation power D = ṡ·φ′(ṡ) of a composite is the sum of the parts' powers, zero for the empty composite and c·D under scaling by c ≥ 0, with every value ≥ 0: a monoid homomorphism into the non-negative reals (Lean: ℝ≥0-linear map dissipationHom)
the atoms (convex ψ with a GSM potential) whose passive balance Δψ + D ≤ 0 holds on one step are closed under sum, non-negative scaling and the empty composite (Lean: a Submodule over ℝ≥0)

a finite non-negative combination of atoms that each pass a passive step passes it, and the composite step satisfies SecondLaw .transition (Lean: also D_total = Σ cᵢ·Dᵢ with each summand ≥ 0; Coq and Agda: list of pre-scaled atoms)
a glue term that is itself a GSM potential composes as an atom with zero free energy: D_glue ≥ 0 and a passive balance with D_total = D_atoms + D_glue satisfies SecondLaw .transition
an arbitrary glue term needs its own witness: under the passive equality balance a negative total dissipation D_atoms + D_glue < 0 is refused by SecondLaw .transition
for non-negative atom and glue dissipations the glue fraction |D_glue| / D_total lies in [0, 1] (Lean and Coq with the division-by-zero convention 0; Agda cross-multiplied: 0 ≤ |D_glue| ≤ D_total)
with non-negative atom dissipation, a glue fraction above one forces D_glue < 0 (Agda cross-multiplied: D_total < |D_glue| forces D_glue < 0)
the capillary porosity of Powers' paste, capillary water plus shrinkage voids, is (w − (w/c)_s·α)/(w + ρ_w/ρ_c) (Agda: p − (w/c)_s·(ρ_c/ρ_w)·(1 − p)·α, the denominator cleared)
the capillary-water coefficient of the rounded closure, (w/c)_s at two decimals, is 0.36
the paste-offset coefficient of the rounded closure, ρ_w/ρ_c at two decimals, is 0.32
the cement volume per unit water volume at unit w/c, ρ_w/ρ_c at three decimals, is 0.317
the rounded capillary-water coefficient lies within 1/200 of (w/c)_s
the rounded paste-offset coefficient lies within 1/200 of ρ_w/ρ_c
